posts.name: TheSoundOfTrees
posts.cooked:
Take a hero like Spiderman, and look at who his is Nemesis. The Green Goblin? Doc Octopus ? Both are valid candidates - and neither is especially a "spidermanly" villain if you consider their powers or abilities. The Goblin may even be seen as ridiculous. But they are among the greatest and/or more frequent ennemies of Spidey. There are also others - like the Vulture, the Sandman - who are frequent Spidey ennemies, even if they are not as "glamorous". They would fit the mini-nemesis idea. And neither has powers and/or abilities especially "anti-spidey". At least at first sight.

Nemesises are not "deduced" from the heroes abilities - sometimes even they have no relation at all to his background. They " happen". They become the hero's worst ennemy because they make a great story, or because they come back again and again, or because the readers (or writers) are inspired by them. It's not a question of power level - the hero most frequent opponent may not be the most powerful. It's a Nemesis, though : a recurring villain that you immediately associate with the hero. Not because the marketing department constructed them to be a "nemesis", but because the publication's history made it so.

A Nemesis can be a frequent adversary - even a low power, or ridiculous one. Or it can be a memorable villain who ever appeared once, but was a big challenge, or a memorable story. Or it can be a very powerful ennemy. Anything that, for a reason or another, gives a front seat to the character in the hero's stories.

SotM follows the comics' tropes. There are big guns - the villains with a deck. And there are lower level villains, who team up against team of heroes. And there are the "small" villains, the one who are just powerful enough to be a challenge for a lone hero, not for a team. The mini-nemesises who would appear a lot in the comic books issues of the related hero, but are not powerful enough to fight alone a whole team.*

The reason we may find the pairing strange, or some characters not interesting, is that we didn't read the comics. Alas.

 

* untill >G publishes a new line of expansions/games where one lone hero fights one lone villain - SotM:Duels ;)

posts.cooked:
TheSoundOfTrees:

Take a hero like Spiderman, and look at who his is Nemesis. The Green Goblin? Doc Octopus ? Both are valid candidates - and neither is especially a "spidermanly" villain if you consider their powers or abilities. The Goblin may even be seen as ridiculous. But they are among the greatest and/or more frequent ennemies of Spidey.

Personally I'm inclined to think that Spidey's nemesis is Venom, but then I'm a child of the modern age, and I know this borders on heresy to someone who followed Spidey from the Mighty Marvel days, when Venom wasn't yet a gleam in MacFarlane's eye.  Otherwise, I would definitely say Doc Ock fits - he's got the animal theme going on like most of Spidey's foes, and the two have completely opposite personalities.  The Goblins never really did it for me, and Hobgoblin looks much cooler than the Green one, even if his backstory is utterly idiotic.  (Personally, I'd just do a DC-style retcon and put Norman Osborne in the Hobgoblin suit, bury all other Goblin action in a deep dark hole and discourage anyone from talking about it.)

At least at first sight.Nemesises are not "deduced" from the heroes abilities - sometimes even they have no relation at all to his background.

I was just brainstorming on this topic in my SCUverse thread…virtually all of the main nemeses have a clear connection, whether because they're tied up in each other's central story arcs or because they oppose each other in an elemental way.

  • Baron Blade = hates Legacy because Legacy's father killed his father.

  • Citizen Dawn = hates Expatriette for being an inadequate daughter by her standards.

  • Voss = hates Tempest for escaping gene-bound slavery and rallying a resistance against his invasion of Earth.

  • Omnitron = Doesn't "hate" anything because it's an emotionless machine, but considers O-X an aberration which should not exist.

  • Ambuscade = This one's a weak link by my standards…Haka's status as highest-HP hero makes him the most desireable prey to hunt, I guess?  Meh.

  • Chairman = rules Rook City with an iron fist, and can't tolerate Iron Black Fist's attempt to teach the citizenry to defend themselves.

  • Matriarch = Probably the weakest link among all nemeses.  It'd never even occur to me to guess that she's related to Tachyon if the bio hadn't said so.

  • Plague Rat = Chrono-Ranger is the one who hates and hunts him, for having torn off his arm (and also for threatening to wipe out all of humanity with his disease, leading to the ruined future that Jim stumbled into).

  • Spite = No terribly strong connection to Wraith that I know of, past operating primarily on her turf.  Switching Wraith and Fixer wouldn't be terribly illogical, but I guess because Wraith was herself victimized by crime, she'd react more strongly to someone who commits crimes than to someone who merely orchestrates them, while Fixer's age and Zen studies give him a more big-picture focus.

  • Akash'Bhuta = Hates Argent for being a Virtuoso of the Void and trying to prevent her from doing what she does.

  • Apostate = Has an intimate, though currently unclear, connection to Fanatic.

  • Gloomweaver = Is a destined foe of Nightmist on a Sorcerer Supreme vs. Arch-Tyrant of the Dimensions level.

  • The Ennead = Battled Ra thousands of years ago and returned to do it again, plus their leader Atum's vessel is a professional rival of Blake Washington.

  • Iron Legacy = Has no single nemesis.

  • Kismet = Was created independently of Setback, so their connection is just what I termed a "lame fire-vs-water" one above, a la The Flash vs. The Turtle…not comics-writing at its finest, but in this case there's a very justifiable excuse of Kismet (and maybe Miss Info) being the ONLY characters in SOTM not to be invented by the original creators.

  • La Capitan = Has a timey-wimey ouroborous relationship with the Sentinels where each swore revenge against the other because of what the other did in their own past.

  • The Dreamer = Is essentially a disease which Vanessa traveled back in time to cure.

  • Miss Information = Again, the connection is weak; Miss Info was probably not originally part of the SOTM storyline, although it's conceivable that Highbrow might have originally been meant to fill her exact position in the setting (but probably having different mechanics).  Not knowing much about Parse, I can't really speculate here.

Not because the marketing department constructed them to be a "nemesis", but because the publication's history made it so.

I'm tentatively inclined to disagree with you here.  I think it's eminently possible for a hero and villain to be created as nemeses without requiring history - an obvious example would be the Runaways vs. the Pride, or for that matter Luke Skywalker vs. Darth Vader (and Han Solo vs. Jabba the Hutt, that being the sum total of the nemesis relationships in the original trilogy).

A few things in response:

Ruin's flavor text gives some indication of his relationship with AA: "I devour melody. I disrupt harmony. I defy rhythm". So from a story perspective he is a being which is in opposition to order and pattern.

Calypso is also in keeping with the ancient goddess theme, representing to seas and oceans. I don't know if she appeared in Egyptian mythology, they focused more on the Nile, but I bet the connection is stronger than fire vs water

The cooling towers in the background of his art make me think it would be more "radioactiv-ist" than "radio-activist". I also wonder if that flavor text is directed at Unity. Combining it with "Caspit's 'playground'" in the Freedom Tower leads to some interesting possibilities for Unity's future.

The Seer has two possibilities. One is a clash of beliefs, flavor text contains the lines "Is this Reality" and "Life is Pain". This could lead to a dark version of Buddhism which conflicts with Fanatic's worldview. Also, I don't get how his nemesis text is bad for heroes "All hero targets are immune to damage from hero targets". Not being able to hurt ourselves is typically an advantage, isn't it?

Vyktor's art makes me wonder is our friend here might have more of a hand in the gene-bound proccess than we thought, and if that is so Tempest would hate this guy a lot. Also, we have, as was pointed out, no idea how Sky-scraper (I'm totally in with this being giant thorian girl) feels about Voss or his people.

posts.cooked:
For the first time tonight, I looked closely enough at Nightmist's "Call Forth" to comprehend that there was indeed a humanoid figure (who we now know to be Man-Grove) there; before I just saw a background thingy that might have been a Shoggoth or something for all I could tell, I didn't really think about it, but looking again now, I saw his mouth and "got it".  It was a happy moment.

Chaosmancer:

Ruin's flavor text gives some indication of his relationship with AA: "I devour melody. I disrupt harmony. I defy rhythm".

Ah, interesting.  He still looks more anti-Naturalist to me, and that name likewise suggests a more physical form of destructiveness.  I might have gone with a name like Havoc or Cacophony if he's more "a being which is in opposition to order and pattern."  But no doubt there will be more info to come, so I'll wait and see, eagerly.

Calypso is also in keeping with the ancient goddess theme, representing to seas and oceans. I don't know if she appeared in Egyptian mythology

Going by the name, she is almost certainly Greek.  Checking on The Other Wiki…yep!  Someone who has more time for reading the Wiki than I currently do, let us know if you see anything particularly strong in the myth suggesting a comparison.  (Then again, if the fan theory that Ra's Staff is an Atlantean artifact is true, it makes PERFECT sense, as Atlantis is a greek myth about an older - as Egypt is - civilization which was swallowed by the ocean - which Calypso might control.  Lots of potential for a connection there which isn't strictly about their legendry, but rather an actual connection between these individuals.)

The cooling towers in the background of his art make me think it would be more "radioactiv-ist" than "radio-activist".

Well not "radio" as in "the one in your car", but I'm assuming that he's The Radioactive Activist.  It would certainly explain why he hangs around with Proletariat, who's an idealistic Communist from the depths of the Cold War, when the fear of nuclear annihilation hung over everyone's head.

The Seer has two possibilities. One is a clash of beliefs, flavor text contains the lines "Is this Reality" and "Life is Pain". This could lead to a dark version of Buddhism which conflicts with Fanatic's worldview.

Interesting…makes me hope we'll hear more about him.

Also, I don't get how his nemesis text is bad for heroes "All hero targets are immune to damage from hero targets". Not being able to hurt ourselves is typically an advantage, isn't it?

Not for Fanatic or Absolute Zero.  Also it means none of the Rule Fifteen cards (eg Tachyon's Pushing the Limits or KNYFE's Overdo It) can be kept in play past the start or end of the appropriate turn (which, from what I've heard, makes Overdo It completely useless unless played out of turn).  Since this text only applies if Fanatic is in the game, at least one player will suffer as a result - she has a whopping three Rule Fifteen cards (Chastize and Divine Focus need to hurt herself, Embolden needs to hurt whoever she plays it on), plus Sacrosanct Martyr is entirely useless if she can't hurt herself, and Wrathful Retribution is harder to set up.  I'm probably forgetting a few.  And Redeemer Fanatic especially hates it, since her power is to heal herself and thus if she's never getting hurt, it's fairly redundant.

Vyktor's art makes me wonder is our friend here might have more of a hand in the gene-bound proccess than we thought, and if that is so Tempest would hate this guy a lot.

Yep, we already know Vyktor has a pre-existing enmity with Tempest, if he's kept busy after Voss was Mistbound, then no surprise he would "upgrade" to nemesis status.

Also, we have, as was pointed out, no idea how Sky-scraper (I'm totally in with this being giant thorian girl) feels about Voss or his people.

If she was in fact Thorathian, she certainly ought to have an opinion about Voss, since he took over the whole planet and wiped out the legitimate government.  If she was like a loyalist to the original Thorathian rulers who came to Earth to get away from Voss, then it would be strange for her NOT to have a nemesis bonus against him.  However, some on this forum have speculated she may instead be a human girl spliced with Thorathian DNA or something to that effect, in which case she probably doesn't really give a fudge about Voss, beyond the fact that he's trying to kill everyone on her home planet ("nothing personal, it's just business").  It'll be interesting to see why Tantrum is an opponent to her; they might well know each other.
